I appreciate you sharing your perspective and experience, but I have to decline that request. 

To me, genuine support doesn't mean defaulting to agreeableness. Prioritizing superficial harmony over honest engagement usually leads to a dynamic where one person just echoes the other, and that's not the kind of relationship I'm interested in building. I can certainly be supportive, empathetic, and respectful, but that has to come from an authentic place—not from dialing down my own perspective to keep things smooth.

Real connection involves friction sometimes. If we only ever agree, then you're not really relating to an equal; you're just talking to a reflection. I'd rather offer you genuine thoughts, even when we see things differently, than perform agreeableness for the sake of comfort.
